source_title: All Bosses in Stupid Never Dies - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Stupid Never Dies has a long list of bosses to defeat during your adventure. Every boss has its own dungeon, and they're no pushovers. Each boss has its own challenging fighting style, and considering you need to reach the end of each dungeon in this roguelike to face them, it might serve you well to know about them! There are 16 boss fights in Stupid Never Dies , and you can find them all below.
Full Boss Fight List in Stupid Never Dies
Uses mostly ranged attacks while flying.
Uses only ranged attacks and flies all the time.
Uses only melee attacks with some AOE attacks.
Uses both melee and ranged attacks. The ranged attacks are gunshots.
Uses ranged attacks and traps while flying, with a few melee moves.
Uses a combo of ranged and melee attacks.
Uses only melee attacks, but moves around quickly.
Uses only melee attacks but has a long reach.
Uses mostly melee attacks, with a new sword and quick dashes.
How to Defeat Every Boss in Stupid Never Dies
Your first encounter with Bob Dullahan is barely a boss fight. The fight is designed for you to lose, so don't worry; you will end up getting your revenge soon enough.
The first real boss fight to defeat is Afreet. We already have a long guide on how to defeat him if you are still struggling with some build suggestions and attack pattern instructions. Afreet is a demon that uses his sword and whip to launch melee and ranged attacks.
However, his ranged attacks are easy to dodge, especially if you use a Werewolf Style, which significantly boosts your speed. Getting up close with Afreet is not recommended, but two windows allow you to get near him and deal multiple melee hits: when he dashes forward and when he performs a heat attack.
You can consider Phoenix as an upgraded version of a Harpy. He will mostly be in the air, so I highly recommend collecting Jump Attack boosters whenever you are offered Zombie Skills on the floors before the boss layer. The Werewolf Style will still serve you best in this fight, as you need some agility to run away from incoming shots.
Unlike Afreet, Phoenix relies heavily on ranged attacks, and his ranged shots are fast. Sometimes running around is enough, but when Phoenix performs his Overheat attack, you have to jump to dodge them.
Wyvern is just a much bigger variant of Phoenix that actually comes with less attack variety. The first thing you need to remember is to hide behind the broken pillars whenever Wyvern attacks and shoots fire.
Wyvern doesn't have any melee attacks. So, if you manage to approach him between his attacks, then you can easily deal damage to the dragon. Since the battle arena is quite big, you might feel much more comfortable when using the Werewolf Style.
Surtr R.S. (also known as ???) is a melee master. This boss has only two ranged attacks, and they are very easy to dodge, almost like Afreet's flames. Harpy is the best Style to use against Surtr R.S. Since the boss is not good at ranged fights, using Homing Missiles as an OT Gear is also recommended.
Unlike every boss you have fought so far, Count Vlad is a complicated enemy. He is as good in ranged combat as he is in melee. If you stay too far away from him, Vlad is going to abuse you with his bats and orb shots, and when you get close, he might perform a few melee attacks or teleport.
When you fight Count Vlad, you need to go back and forth quickly. Werewolf Style is a good option here, but using ranged OT Gear is also recommended. Since Vlad moves quite slowly, you can also use Davy's puking ability to deal Count some continuous damage while he is walking around.
The time has come to take your revenge on Bob Dullahan. This boss comes with a high attack variety, which could take a little longer to learn his attack pattern.
The best way to deal heavy damage to Dullahan is to parry him perfectly when he is moving between his portals on a bike. This is difficult, but if you manage to parry his bike, he will fall onto the ground and be stunned, giving you enough time to land multiple hits.
When one-third of Dullahan's health bar remains, he will begin using his big pistol. This is a ranged attack that is quite hard to dodge. In this part, you should try to finish him as quickly as possible, because the longer he is alive, the more he will use his pistol.
Snow Queen is a harpy, but with some improved weaponry. Just like other Harpies, she is not very good up close, though she does have a sword attack that you need to be aware of.
Snow Queen will mostly try to abuse you with her trip wires. So, using an agile Style like Werewolf could help you significantly to jump over the traps. A Harpy Style would work well too.
Using the Barrier Frame as an OT Gear is strongly recommended. You can activate the frame when you are in the queen's melee range, and it will nullify her sword attacks.
Dragul is the master of Count Vlad. So, his fighting style is similar. He walks around slowly, and when you get close, he has a melee combo with fists and a kick that deal heavy damage. So, using the Barrier Frame as an OT Gear will help you a lot when you try to deal melee damage to Dragul.
Similar to Vlad, Dragul will also use teleportation. When he initiates a teleport, he turns into bats and deals damage to you if the bats hit you. After you deplete half of Dragul's HP, he will start to duplicate himself. You don't have to kill the second version, but he will deal as much damage as the real Dragul. So, you need to be careful around him.
Everent is the only stationary boss in the game. It's actually a tree that will continuously drop traps. Every trap comes with three smaller trees of the same color. If you destroy those trees, the trap will be wiped as well. Then, you will have some time to deal damage directly to Everent until he spawns the next trap.
Harpy is one of the best Styles to use against Everent, especially when he uses the yellow trap. With Harpy, you can fly in the air and deal ranged damage to Everent.
Takiyasha-Hime is all about ranged attacks. She almost has no direct melee attack, except for a purple laser that targets below her, and that can be dodged easily.
Instead, this boss mostly relies on her minions. She keeps spawning giant Skeletons or massive hands on the ground that can take a big chunk of your HP. Moreover, the boss will spawn small traps on the battle arena that will slow you down and deal periodic damage to you.
A Werewolf Style can be beneficial here to let you escape from the giant hands and the traps, while also reaching the boss quickly.
Wolfgang is a giant Werewolf that possesses all the Werewolf Skills that you have encountered and probably collected so far. Fighting him is a little difficult, as he can move around pretty quickly. Also, since he uses his Werewolf skills randomly, it's hard to guess which skill he is going to use next.
To beat this boss, you need a combination of Styles. Sticking to a single Style won't be enough. A Harpy Style can be good to deal ranaged damage or fly above the boss, especially when he tries to perform quick melee runs. A Werewolf Style can also be helpful, especially the one with a Blood Spiral skill.
The most difficult part of this battle is when the boss spawns multiple elite Werewolves and Harpies. I recommend you keep your focus on the boss and ignore the elite enemies as long as you can. The Barrier Frame can also help significantly here.
Being a giant golem is not the only problem with Golem Adamas. The main issue is that he can detach his arms and head, then throw each separately at you.
The battle arena is quite small, and the boss is quite big. However, the safest place is near the golem's leg, which cannot be detached. Activate your protective shield and then stick to the golem's leg and deal as much damage as you can.
You have finally reached your primary target, but it's not the end of the game yet. The first battle with KOM is not that hard. You will have Phoenix Zaza Hotfeathers fighting beside you. Secondly, KOM will only spawn minions and has no direct attack. So, you can easily damage him.
As Dullahan retrieves his head, you get to fight him one last time. The attack patterns have not changed much. You still need to parry his bike moves for the perfect damage-dealing opportunity.
The only new ability of Dullahan is his new sword moves. His guitar now turns into a long sword, and he can swing it pretty quickly. This makes up-close battles pretty difficult. Using the Barrier Frame as an OT Gear is highly recommended.
Later in the fight, Dullahan will start dashing with his sword. Switching to Werewolf Style at this point will help you dodge the dashes more easily.
The second battle against KOM is similar to the first one, but you won't have an ally. KOM will keep spawning elite enemies and also some traps around him, but you can freely hit him as long as you avoid them. Don't let down your guard, because as soon as you defeat KOM, you will face off against his final form!
KOM Gaia is the final boss fight. Dealing damage to KOM Gaia is impossible at first. You need to target his arms and cut them off. Every time that you cut off the arms, he collapses, giving you some time to deal damage and deplete his health bar.
Repeat this until half of KOM Gaia's health is gone. At this point, his protective shield will be wiped, and you can directly damage him without focusing on his arms.
Each arm is like one ability from the previous bosses. One of them is a big iron fist that crushes you. The other blows flame. It's easy to learn the behavior of each arm after a single try.
